back: Greater vigour or yield of F1 offspring of genetically different parents (hybrid vigour).
Nearly homozygous line made by self-pollinating for several generations; uniform but weak.
Single: A × B. Three-way: (A × B) × C. Double: (A × B) × (C × D).

front: Why buy hybrid seed each season?
back: Grain is F2: alleles segregate, plants vary and lose hybrid vigour, so yields fall.
Open: natural, pollen parent unknown. Controlled: breeder chooses pollen (bagging, detasselling).
Yield, pest and disease resistance, hardiness (drought, heat), early maturity, quality, uniformity.
It is produced on a weak inbred female that yields little seed.
Selective: cross related plants and select over generations. GM: insert chosen genes directly, even from other species.
(F1 yield − mean of parents) ÷ mean of parents × 100.
